title: Walkable 3D Kyoto neighborhood in Three.js
author: God of Prompt
verification: Fetched from X via twitter-cli from global-search; original author and post URL preserved.
note: Original post did not expose a complete repeatable prompt. Treat this as a real showcase post, not a verified tutorial.
originalText:
I had Claude Fable 5 build a walkable 3D Kyoto neighborhood in Three.js. Runs in the browser.

It's not a single street. There's a connected grid of alleys, intersections, and plazas you can actually wander through. Machiya townhouses, stone lanterns, cherry blossoms, paper lanterns glowing at dusk. A pagoda visible above the rooflines from different streets.

Golden hour and night mode toggle. WASD to walk. Mouse to look around.

Took two prompts. One for the initial build, one to fix the layout so it wasn't a straight corridor. Some areas still feel disconnected and disjointed, but for a browser-rendered 3D neighborhood from two prompts, it's not bad.

title: App prototype built with Fable 5

originalText:
Just pushed Small Harness 0.7.0 to Github, calling this one the observability release. And my first release built with Claude Fable.

Two big things: a flight recorder for your agent, and evals you can run from a shell script.

Turn tracing: every session gets an .events.jsonl sidecar tool calls (args redacted), approvals, compaction, warmup, timing. /trace on shows nested subagent/critic activity live. Your turn footer now breaks down TTFT vs model vs tools vs approval time.

 Agent eval CLI: --eval <fixture> --json runs a bundled task end-to-end and exits 0/1. Plus new integration tests that drive the real agent loop against a mock SSE server, no live LLM needed.

Also: sharper tool responses for the model (clear EOF errors, real totals on truncated listings), 10s connect timeout so dead backends fail fast, and a big internal cleanup. 

To use: brew upgrade small-harness 🍺

And as always, Github repo in first comment below. Free, open source, use it as it is, or fork it and go nuts.
